name: run-error-then-new-run-continues
description: RUN_ERROR does not end the stream: a RUN_STARTED after it begins a new run in the same stream, and everything the second run produces is applied and delivered
kill: drop the RUN_ERROR arm from resetRunState's caller in verifyEvents so a RUN_STARTED after a RUN_ERROR is rejected as nested, or make the reducer's RUN_ERROR case end the stream (a `throwError` after `emitUpdates()`) — either way the second run's message never arrives and `messages`, `eventTypes` and `outcome` fail together

dotnet.intentional: The .NET client's event surface is ChatResponseUpdate.RawRepresentation, and the builder-only events yield no update: TEXT_MESSAGE_START and TEXT_MESSAGE_END open and close the message being assembled and hand a consumer nothing, so they cannot appear in a delivered list however faithfully the client processed them. `eventTypes` is restated without them; everything else the base asserts — the restart itself, the second run's runId at the same index, the message it produced, the reported run failure and the silence — holds unchanged.
